document.title: Pakistan Afghan Policy: Anyone but Rabbani/Massoud - Even the Taliban (Islama 09675)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] Pakistan's Ambassador to Afghanistan Qazi Humayun says Pakistan finds itself in the uncomfortable position of backing the Taliban. Relations with the Rabbani government had worsened after a mob destroyed Pakistan's embassy in Kabul in September. Humayun says a Taliban government would in many ways be worse than the present one.

persons.name: Qazi Humayun
persons.status_detail: severely beaten during the 6 Sep 1995 sacking of the Pakistani embassy in Kabul

mentions.quote: PAK AMBASSADOR TO AFGHANISTAN QAZI HUMAYUN EXPLAINED THAT IN THE WAKE OF LAST MONTH'S SACKING OF THE PAK EMBASSY IN KABUL
DURING WHICH HUMAYUN WAS SEVERELY BEATEN
HUMAYUN SAID THAT "IN A COUPLE OF DAYS" HE PLANS TO GO TO JALALABAD TO "OPEN A SMALL, LOW-KEY PRESENCE."

persons.name: Rabbani

events.description: Government-sanctioned sacking of the Pakistani Embassy in Kabul; Ambassador Humayun severely beaten.
Pakistan expelled Ambassador Khalili and several Afghan diplomats.
Charge and Poloff met Ambassador Humayun; Pakistan expelled another batch of Afghan diplomats the same day.
Afghan government-sanctioned sacking of the Pakistan Embassy in Kabul; Ambassador Humayun was severely beaten.
Pakistan declared Afghan Ambassador Khalili and other Afghan diplomats persona non grata.
Ambassador Humayun met the US Charge and Poloff in a wide-ranging conversation on Pakistan's Afghan policy.
GOP expelled another batch of Afghan diplomats, including the charge d'affaires.
An American with over 20 years' Afghanistan experience voiced concerns about Taliban heavy-handedness in Herat, echoed by Humayun.
Humayun planned to go to Jalalabad within days to open a low-key Pakistani presence.
Foreign Minister Aseff Ali toured Afghanistan in summer 1995, including a stop in Kabul.

sources_cited: Conversation with Ambassador Qazi Humayun, 17 Oct 1995
Observations of an American with 20+ years' Afghanistan experience, 16 Oct 1995
key_claims: Pakistani policy was driven by domestic opposition to the Kabul government after the 6 Sep 1995 embassy sacking.
Pakistan found itself backing the Taliban reluctantly.
Humayun considered a Taliban government potentially worse than the current one and a poor neighbor.
The Taliban saw no incentive to form an alliance with Dostam or the Supreme Coordinating Council.
The Taliban were heavy-handed in Herat on schools and women's work.
Pakistan planned a Jalalabad presence that could enable a parallel government if the battle for Kabul stalemated.
